lf-timeline.description: An authored sequence of events over time, one lane per actor, that the reader steps through with Previous and Next while a playhead and a step list follow. Use it to explain an order of events, such as a race between jobs; use `lf-trace` for a recorded browser journey and `lf-motion` for continuous playback.
lf-timeline.x-instructions: Write one `lf-lane` per actor, in the order the reader should scan them, and in each an `lf-event` per thing that happened to it. `at` is the event's time in milliseconds from the sequence's start; add `end` for an event with duration, such as work in progress, and leave it out for an instant. Previous and Next visit events in start order: events with the same `at` share one step, and a span's end is not a step, so model a moment the reader must stop at, such as a write landing, as its own instant. Keep each `label` to a short clause, since the prose around the widget carries the explanation; the widget lays labels out so that none overlaps a bar, another label or the playhead. Give every event a page-unique `id`: it is the event's comment target.
lf-timeline.x-example: <lf-timeline id="deploy-order" aria-label="Deploy order"><lf-lane label="Build"><lf-event id="deploy-compile" at="0" end="4000" label="Compile"></lf-event><lf-event id="deploy-artifact" at="4000" label="Artifact ready"></lf-event></lf-lane><lf-lane label="Release"><lf-event id="deploy-rollout" at="4500" end="9000" label="Roll out"></lf-event></lf-lane></lf-timeline>

lf-lane.description: One actor's row in an `lf-timeline`, holding its events.

lf-event.description: One event in a timeline lane: an instant at `at`, or a span from `at` to `end`, in milliseconds.
